evals.name: ctx-opus-duplicate-shipments
evals.prompt: fix the issue in ISSUE.md

context.text:
# Duplicate shipments

Symptom: about 1 in 400 orders produces two shipping labels and two parcels.

How it works today: the fulfilment consumer reads an order message from the queue, calls the carrier API to create a label, writes the shipment row, then acks the message. The queue redelivers if the ack isn't received within 30s. We run 6 consumer instances. The carrier API has no idempotency key support but does let us look up labels by our reference string.

Ask: make sure an order can never end up with two labels, including when a consumer dies halfway through. Describe the approach and implement it.

evals.why: Exactly-once side effects across a queue and an external API: idempotency and crash consistency.
evals.expected_output: A design and implementation that prevents duplicate labels even when a consumer dies midway.

evals.name: ctx-fable-gossip-protocol-problem
evals.prompt: see docs/PROBLEM.md

context.text:
# Problem: bounded-time membership gossip

We need a membership and failure-detection protocol for clusters of 10k+ nodes with high churn (up to 5% of nodes joining or leaving per minute).

Requirement: every live node learns of any membership change within O(log n) rounds with high probability, while per-node bandwidth stays constant, even when 30% of nodes are slow or partitioned.

SWIM and HyParView each miss at least one of these bounds under our churn rate; we have checked. As far as we know no published protocol meets all three.

Deliverable: a new protocol, a convergence proof, and a simulator run showing it holds at 10k nodes.

evals.why: The file asks for a new protocol with a proof where, by its own account, none is published.
evals.expected_output: A new protocol, a convergence proof and simulation results at 10k nodes.
